name: Patch three random-gate tools from generic functions: noise sampled-and-held by a clock into a window comparator, ANDed with the clock, as a probability gate skipper (window size = probability); the same with S&H output fed back into the clock rate for free random bursts; and a Bernoulli gate where comparator out and not-out each AND the clock to trigger two panned voices
goal: Make random and probabilistic gates without dedicated modules. Raw noise into a window comparator gives random gates, but only at a very small window size and with no sync or range. Instead, sample-and-hold the noise on a clock and feed the held value to the comparator: keep shift (window position) high so only the top of the held voltage range passes, and use window size as the probability control (max = all pass, fully closed = none). Because the comparator only fires when the window opens, AND its output with the original clock so every clock passes at maximum. For free random bursts, feed the S&H output back into the clock's rate CV for an unsteady clock. For a Bernoulli gate, use the comparator's out and not-out, each ANDed with the clock (a VCA works as AND), to trigger two envelopes on a higher voice panned left and a lower voice panned right; size then sets the odds of left vs right and they never fire together. Modulate size with a slow LFO and add clock feedback for a generative patch. Maps to Polyrhythm Studio as per-step random gating lanes.

source.title: Patch Programmability - Episode 4 - Random Gate Generators
source.transcript_note: Modular patching tutorial; channel CTA dropped; module names kept only as functions.

prerequisites: Modular, semi-modular or software modular with noise, sample-and-hold, a window comparator (with not-output, or logic to invert), AND logic or VCAs, a clock/cycling function generator, envelopes and VCAs, or Web Audio / JS: on each clock tick sample r=Math.random(); pass if r falls in [shift-size/2, shift+size/2]; Bernoulli: route to voice A if in window else voice B (implementation note)
Two oscillator voices tuned high and low

inputs.name: clock
inputs.description: Steady clock (or one with rate CV for the free-random variant)

inputs.name: window_shift
inputs.description: Window position; keep high in the skipper patch

outputs.name: random_gate_patch
outputs.description: Gate skipper / random burst / Bernoulli patch

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Unclocked noise into a comparator works only at very small window sizes; open it slightly and gates reach audio rate.
Without the AND with the clock, some gates are dropped even at maximum probability (the comparator stays high across consecutive in-window samples, and S&H sampling is not instantaneous).
Using raw out/not-out in the Bernoulli patch can let both outputs fire on one clock; the extra AND stage fixed this in the video.
The size knob's mapping to probability is not calibrated (roughly 50/50 near the middle). Module brands are not required; functions only.

steps.action: Run noise into a window comparator; trigger an envelope → VCA on a voice from the comparator output. Set window size very low and move shift.
steps.expect: Random gates, but only usable in a narrow knob range and unsynced

steps.action: Add sample-and-hold: noise into S&H input, a cycling clock into S&H clock, S&H output into the comparator. Set shift high so only the top of the held range passes.
steps.expect: Random gates aligned to the clock

steps.action: AND the comparator output with the original clock (second comparator, logic module, or a VCA with clock as input and comparator as CV). Use window size as the probability: max = all clocks pass, closed = none. Listen against a second voice playing the raw clock.
steps.expect: A probability gate skipper; skipped clocks are audible against the reference

steps.action: Free random variant: patch the S&H output into the clock's rate CV.

Bernoulli variant: remove the feedback; take comparator out and not-out, AND each with a copy of the clock, and send them to two envelopes: one on a higher voice panned slightly left, one on a lower voice panned slightly right.
steps.expect: Each clock goes to exactly one of the two voices

steps.action: Sweep size: fully clockwise = only the high voice, fully counter-clockwise = only the low voice, middle = random choice. Then modulate size with a slow LFO and add clock-rate feedback for a generative patch.

verification: In the skipper at maximum size every clock passes; at minimum none pass.
In the Bernoulli patch the two voices never trigger on the same clock.
With S&H → clock-rate feedback the gate intervals are uneven.
Window size in the middle gives a roughly even split between the two voices.
